title: The Recycling Truck
strapline: Empty the bins, sort the load, drive it away — the crew who keep the whole street working.
intent: The recycling and bin lorry is a working vehicle children see every week, and playing it lets them replay and understand a real, important job in their community.
Sorting recycling into the right bins — paper here, cans there, glass over there — is genuine classification with a real-world purpose.
Collecting, lifting, emptying and driving is big, satisfying physical work with a clear sequence of stops and jobs.
The play opens honest conversations about looking after our world, waste, reusing and why the crew's work matters.
Naming the crew, the truck and its parts, and talking about the round, builds vocabulary and respect for the people who help us.
Counting bins, loads and stops weaves number naturally through a purposeful, familiar storyline.
implementation: Set up bins or boxes for different materials and a truck (a ride-on, trolley or small-world lorry) to collect and empty them.
Provide real, clean recyclables to sort — cardboard, plastic bottles, cans, paper — and agree together which goes where.
Play alongside as a resident with a full bin, or a tricky mixed-up load, to stretch the sorting and the talk.
Narrate the round: 'first stop, empty the paper — next house, what have they got out today?'
Talk simply about why we recycle and reuse, drawing out children's own ideas about caring for the world.
Watch the real lorry on its round if you can, then replay what the crew actually did.
key_questions: First stop, empty the paper — next house, what have they got out today?
Paper here, cans there, glass over there — where does this go?
How many bins have we emptied so far?
Why do you think we recycle instead of throwing it all away?
What could this old box become instead?

playing_exploring: Children collect, sort and empty with big, purposeful movements, replaying a job they see every week.
Real recyclables to sort make the classifying genuine and hands-on.
active_learning: Working the round — stop, empty, sort, drive on — is absorbing work children see through to the end.
creating_thinking: Children sort by material and reason about why, and solve the puzzles a mixed-up or overflowing load throws up.
